question: An article marked at ₹500 is sold for ₹425. What is the percentage discount?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Discount = Marked Price − Selling Price.

Discount = 500 − 425 = ₹75.

Discount % = (Discount ÷ Marked Price) × 100.

Discount % = (75 ÷ 500) × 100 = 15%.

**∴ The correct answer is 15%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹500

Selling Price (SP) = ₹425

**Formula Used:**

Discount = MP − SP

Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the equivalent single discount is [a + b − (a × b ÷ 100)]%.

Relation between CP and MP

When Profit % (P) and Discount % (D) are both given, the ratio of Marked Price to Cost Price is MP ÷ CP = (100 + P) ÷ (100 − D).

Mark Up Percentage

Mark up percentage is calculated over the Cost Price. Mark Up % = [(MP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100.
